summary: A detailed guide to connecting an EU Freestyle Libre 2/2+ directly to xDrip over Bluetooth using the OOP2 app: starting the sensor with LibreLink, pairing it in xDrip, checking the connection and troubleshooting. All steps happen in xDrip, OOP2, LibreLink and Android; no AAPS screen is used.

sections.heading: How to Start a FSL2 Sensor in Bluetooth Native mode using LL and xDrip
sections.summary: Introduces the numbered steps; settings shown unchecked in the screenshots must stay off.

sections.heading: Step 1: Application Installation and Configuration
sections.summary: Installing and checking OOP2 and xDrip. All settings named are xDrip's or OOP2's.

sections.heading: Step 2: xDrip Settings Configuration
sections.summary: xDrip settings for native Libre 2 Bluetooth, optionally loaded from a QR code with xDrip's Auto Configure, plus OOP2 settings. xDrip labels only.

sections.heading: Step 3: Physically insert the sensor
sections.summary: Inserting the sensor.

sections.heading: Step 4: Start the LL App and start sensor with very first NFC Scan
sections.summary: Starting the sensor with one LibreLink NFC scan, then closing or uninstalling LibreLink and waiting out the 60-minute warm-up.

sections.heading: Step 4a (OPTIONAL, Use FSLReader):
sections.summary: Starting the sensor with the FreeStyle reader first so the reader can also be used, and keeping LibreLink from taking the Bluetooth connection.

sections.heading: Step 5: Open xDrip and NFC SCAN the FSL2 sensor
sections.summary: Scanning the sensor with xDrip's NFC to begin Bluetooth bonding.

sections.heading: Step 6: Start the new sensor in xDrip
sections.summary: Starting the sensor from xDrip's menu and answering 'Not today' to the insertion prompt.

sections.heading: Step 7: Wait 60 seconds and NFC Scan the sensor again
sections.summary: A second xDrip NFC scan, a minute later, adds the sensor as xDrip's Bluetooth device; check xDrip's event log.

sections.heading: Step 8: Data Collection between 3 and 15 Minutes
sections.summary: Waiting for the first readings and, on some phones, applying a QR code that changes xDrip's Bluetooth settings.

sections.heading: Step 9: Verify Sensor is connected and delivering data
sections.summary: Checking the connection on xDrip's System Status and BT Device screens; the field names and states are xDrip's, not AAPS labels.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.summary: Using LibreLink scans after bonding, phone reboots, excluding xDrip, OOP2, LibreLink and AndroidAPS from battery optimisation, and flight mode.

sections.heading: Advantages
sections.summary: Benefits of this method: no patched LibreLink, no third-party NFC bridge, reader still usable, fewer devices, no gaps at sensor change.

sections.heading: Disadvantages
sections.summary: Drawbacks: care after reboots, LibreLink and xDrip cannot share Bluetooth, reader must start the sensor, no automatic LibreView upload.

sections.heading: Failure to scan the sensor with NFC
sections.summary: Fixes for NFC scans that fail: phone NFC settings, antenna position, xDrip's NFC reading options.

sections.heading: Stuck on collecting initial readings
sections.summary: Setting OOP2's calibration strategy to 'No calibration' until readings arrive. This is an OOP2 option, not the AAPS calibration plugin.

sections.heading: Sensor is reported as FSL1
sections.summary: Update xDrip and OOP2.

sections.heading: Connection to the sensor fails
sections.summary: Checks when xDrip cannot connect: OOP1 off, OOP2 not put to sleep, Play Protect off, Bluetooth Pairing back to Disabled in xDrip's System Status.

sections.summary: Signs of a failing sensor in OOP2 values and xDrip's sensor age.
